gaps.note: Sudden cut to the founder smiling as Kevin interrupts, hiding the immediate reaction to Robert's offer.

stage_a.note: She smiles warmly and uses engaging gestures while presenting her product with clear positive engagement.
She speaks with clear animation and passion about creating a non-alcoholic option for social settings.
She is highly approachable and invites the sharks to join her with open arms and a smile.

venture.description: A non-alcoholic, all-natural aperitif that offers a complex, bitter flavor profile akin to Campari, designed for social drinking without the alcohol.
venture.note: She sells direct to consumer and to restaurant accounts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder introduces herself, states her ask, and pitches her non-alcoholic aperitif designed for social settings.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how they should drink the product and expresses a desire to try it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert suggests they have a drink together and prepares to taste it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the different ready-made spritzes and their flavor profiles.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert expresses positive surprise upon tasting the beverage.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many calories are in the drink.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states there are about 50 calories.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks for clarification if that is for the whole can.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms that the calorie count is for the whole can.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert compliments the drink and states he loves it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains that the drink is meant to be a non-alcoholic amaro, similar to Campari.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert agrees that it reminds him of Campari.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder notes it is an all-natural and lighter version.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin praises the taste of the drink in French.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks Kevin in French.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if the drink contains bitters.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert also praises the drink in French.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks about the retail price and the cost to make each product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder details the retail prices and manufacturing costs for both the bottles and the spritzes.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark shifts the topic to the business and asks to hear their sales numbers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder reveals they made 2.5 million dollars in their first calendar year, mostly online due to the pandemic.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark expresses being very impressed by the high sales number.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks to confirm the 2.5 million dollar sales figure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks if they made any profit on those sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains how they launched via an Instagram post and gained traction quickly.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori again asks for confirmation that it sold 2.5 million.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert repeats the question of whether they made any money on the sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they are not yet profitable as they invested heavily for growth.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much money they lost last year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder reveals they lost a little under a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks for confirmation of the one million dollar loss.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder clarifies that they hold a million dollars worth of inventory.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much capital they have raised.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they raised 3.5 million and are currently raising another 6.5 million.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark expresses surprise at the large amount of money raised.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks what the valuation was for the 3.5 million dollar raise.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the first 900,000 was a SAFE at a 7.5 million dollar cap.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks who invested the initial 900,000 pre-revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder says it was people she previously worked for at companies like Sweetgreen and Goldman Sachs.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks how much of the business she still owns.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms she still owns 57% of the business after the current round.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert notes that her retained ownership percentage is impressive.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks about the valuation for the current 6.5 million dollar round.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder reveals it is a 35 million dollar pre-money valuation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert expresses shock at the high valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark calculates and confirms that it implies a 41 million dollar post-money valuation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks what her projected sales are for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder projects 4.5 million in sales, planning to double it the following year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that he needs a real alcoholic drink after hearing the numbers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert challenges why she is offering the panel a 5 million valuation when she is raising at 40 million.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the equity comes from her personal shares to secure their help in building a huge business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark commends her strategy of offering personal shares as smart.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder elaborates on her personal hustle to get the product into 750 accounts and her vision for the future.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond praises her impressiveness but exits because his acid reflux prevents him from drinking the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder politely thanks Daymond.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori exits because she cannot consume citrus or bitter things and needs to partake in products she invests in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder politely thanks Lori.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark exits because he believes the beverage category is too difficult and expensive to scale.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder politely thanks Mark.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert agrees with Mark about the category's difficulty but praises her for killing it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert makes an offer to invest exactly what she asked for.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin interjects, asking her to wait before accepting.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert warns her that Kevin might make an offer since he is in the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Kevin if he is in the wine business.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin confirms he is in the wine business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert jokes that there is no alcohol in this product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks the founder if she wants to hear his offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert demands she accept his exact-ask offer immediately or he will step out to let her negotiate with Kevin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states she feels it is only fair to hear everyone out.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark agrees that her desire to hear all offers is reasonable.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert withdraws his offer and exits because she did not accept it immediately.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin reacts to Robert withdrawing his offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert reiterates that he gave her exactly what she asked for.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark tells the founder that Robert is right about giving her what she asked for.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert justifies his withdrawal, questioning why entrepreneurs come if they won't take what they asked for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder politely thanks Robert.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin makes an offer but demands 10% equity, claiming he is too valuable for 5%.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert points out that Kevin's offer just crushed her valuation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin argues he has to work on it and blames Robert for costing her a better deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks the founder what she thinks of Kevin's offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder rejects the offer, explaining she cannot accept a lower valuation without wronging her early supporters.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin argues she has enough equity to accept it, maintaining his demand for 10%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms that she is honored but cannot accept the offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin respects her decision.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori wishes the founder good luck.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks the panel before leaving.

decisions.note: He cannot drink it because he has acid reflux.
She cannot eat citrus or bitter things.
The category is one of the hardest and most expensive to scale.
He offers exactly what she asked for because she is killing it.
He withdraws because she wants to hear other offers instead of accepting immediately.
He wants 10% because he is in the business and considers his value higher.
She cannot accept the lower valuation without wronging her early supporters.
She confirms she cannot accept his 10% offer.
